body: I got random results from `{foo.bar > 99 ? 'less' : 'more'}` too, but I'm not sure if it's related to this issue or the #13106 one.

I can confirm that we fail to parse `{#if (foo.bar == 'something') || (foo.bar == 'other')}` and that's a bug. However, I get consistent (and correct) results for `{#if foo.bar == 'something' || foo.bar == 'other'}`. Can you describe your use case in more details or even better - could you provide a test?

`{foo.bar > 99 ? 'less' : 'more'}` is not supported ATM and [it's documented](https://quarkus.io/guides/qute-reference#built-in-operators).
It was actually `{#if foo.bar != 'something' && foo.bar != 'other'}` that didn't work, I checked. Apparently the first expression was ignored and only the second test was taken into account.

@FroMage Wait a minute, if `bar` is `something` then the first part of the condition is `false` and thus `NOK` should be rendered, or? I'm a bit slow today so I'm probably missing something obvious...
Haha, yes, sorry you're right. My point was that in my experience, when `bar` was `something` I still got `OK` instead of the `NOK` I was expecting.

>  My point was that in my experience, when bar was something I still got OK instead of the NOK I was expecting.

I will add a bunch of tests but I don't know how this could happen...
